title: Events and describe: what Kubernetes did
summary: Read a broken workload from the cluster's own account of it: STATUS, describe, events sorted by time.

steps.title: Start from what the cluster saw
body: Every debugging session on Kubernetes starts with three read-only commands, in this order:
kubectl get pods -o wide                       # the state: STATUS, READY, RESTARTS, NODE
kubectl describe pod NAME                      # the object plus its Events at the bottom
kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp    # the namespace's timeline (newest last)
**Events** are written by the scheduler, the kubelet and the controllers when they act or fail:
`FailedCreate` (a ReplicaSet rejected by a quota). The REASON plus the message is usually the whole diagnosis.
Two details seniors rely on: events are kept for about an hour only, and `kubectl events --for pod/NAME --types=Warning`
(the newer command) filters to one object's problems.

steps.prompt: `kubectl get pods` shows `ImagePullBackOff`. Where do you find the exact image reference and the registry's error message?
options: The Events of `kubectl describe pod NAME` (`Failed to pull image ...`)
steps.explain: The container never started, so it has no logs. The kubelet records each pull attempt and its error as events on the pod: `not found` (a typo in the tag), `unauthorized` (a missing `imagePullSecret`), or a timeout (registry or network).

steps.prompt: Match the event REASON to what it means.
pairs: no node fits the pod's requests, selectors or taints
image pulls keep failing; the kubelet waits longer each time
a liveness, readiness or startup probe failed
pods were rejected at admission (quota, policy)

steps.title: Fix an ImagePullBackOff
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). A release of `web` went out and its new pods never start:
1. Find the image reference that cannot be pulled (in the pod's events), and write it into `~/answers/image.txt`.
2. Fix the Deployment's image to the version that exists here (`traefik/whoami:v1.11`) and wait for the rollout.

checks.name: image.txt has the broken reference
checks.fail: Not the broken image. `kubectl describe pod` on a new pod: `Failed to pull image "..."`.

checks.name: web is rolled out on v1.11
checks.cmd: kubectl rollout status deploy/web --timeout=40s >/dev/null; kubectl get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image} {.status.readyReplicas} {.status.updatedReplicas}'
checks.fail: `web` should run `traefik/whoami:v1.11` with 2 ready, updated pods.

hints: `kubectl get pods`, then `kubectl describe pod NAME` on one of the failing pods: read the last Events.
`kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -i pull` shows the same messages for the whole namespace.
`kubectl set image deploy/web whoami=traefik/whoami:v1.11`, then `kubectl rollout status deploy/web`.
solution: kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -i 'failed to pull' | tail -n 1
steps.explain: `ImagePullBackOff` is the kubelet backing off after `ErrImagePull`; the event message says why (here `not found`: `1l` instead of `11`). Because the rollout only replaced pods as fast as new ones became ready, the old ones kept serving the whole time. `kubectl set image` started a new revision with the right tag.

steps.prompt: A Deployment's pods are `Pending` and `describe` says `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector`. What do you change?
options: The pod's `nodeSelector`/affinity, or the node's labels, so they match
steps.explain: The scheduler lists every reason it rejected each node. A selector mismatch is quiet: the YAML is valid and the pod just waits. `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` shows what the nodes offer.
